summary.text: St. Lawrence was an archdeacon of Rome, remembered for care of the poor and martyrdom during the persecution under Valerian.
summary.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

saints.context: The source’s received ecclesiastical narrative is identified as such. Uncertain dates, later traditions and unknown circumstances of death are retained as uncertain.

blocks.text: St. Lawrence, also spelled Laurence, served as archdeacon in the Church of Rome during the third-century persecution under Valerian. The OCA commemorates him with fellow Roman martyrs and places their suffering in 258.
blocks.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

blocks.text: In the received life, his imprisoned bishop entrusts the Church’s valuables to him for distribution to people in need. When officials demand the treasury, St. Lawrence brings poor people before them. The story makes his diaconal responsibility for charitable service central to his witness.
blocks.locator: Distribution of treasures and presentation of the poor

sourceRefs.locator: Distribution of treasures and presentation of the poor

blocks.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

blocks.text: The OCA account says that he refuses to sacrifice to idols and undergoes repeated torture. It describes his final execution on a heated iron gridiron on August 10, 258. The details are presented as the Church’s received martyrdom narrative; this profile introduces no new speech or reconstructed dialogue.
blocks.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

blocks.text: The life recounts the honorable burial of his body and the later presence of relics in Rome and other Orthodox locations. His Orthodox commemoration brings an early western martyr into the same calendar of witness as the martyrs of the East.
blocks.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.
